comment: The introduction appropriately describes the architecture as adaptive and non-prescriptive. However, “engage with at the level that is relevant to them” is vague and does not explain whether countries may omit components, alter relationships, or redefine component boundaries.

anchor.note: p.24 l.Lines 3-11 read as the printed page; section 2 does NOT agree

public.text: The introduction appropriately describes the architecture as adaptive and non-prescriptive. However, “engage with at the level that is relevant to them” is vague and does not explain whether countries may omit components, alter relationships, or redefine component boundaries.
public.suggestedRevision: Clarify the permissible forms of adaptation. For example: “Countries may adopt, adapt, combine, federate, or defer individual components, provided that the capabilities, interfaces, governance responsibilities, and resulting deviations are explicitly documented.”
